description.summary: keyboard shortcuts inhibition for the window manager

protocol.description:
This fork-only protocol (newm-river, a fork of river) carries what the window manager needs for keyboard-shortcuts-inhibit-unstable-v1, which river serves to clients: river activates every inhibitor a client creates for its surface (as niri does), and while the surface with a seat's keyboard focus holds an active inhibitor, river matches none of that seat's river_xkb_binding_v1 objects but the ones the window manager marked not inhibitable, and sends the keys to the focused client instead. A VM viewer or a remote desktop then gets Super and Alt+Tab.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.

interface.name: newm_river_shortcuts_v1
interface.description: This global interface should only be advertised to the client if the river_window_manager_v1 global is also advertised.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The client will no longer use the newm_river_shortcuts_v1 object. Bindings keep the inhibitable state last set.

request.name: set_inhibitable

description.summary: whether an inhibitor holds back a binding

request.description: A binding is inhibitable when it is created: an active inhibitor on the focused surface keeps it from matching. A binding set not inhibitable (0) still matches, so the window manager keeps a way to toggle the inhibitor off or lock the session. Ignored for an inert binding.

request.name: toggle_inhibit
request.description: Deactivate the inhibitor of the surface with the seat's keyboard focus when it is active, activate it when it is not. Nothing happens when that surface holds no inhibitor or the seat is inert.
